chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all together from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymoun, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He mentioned the oil of violet, so he purified it, then said: 'And the gillyflower oil is gentle.'

key_terms.فَزَكَّاهُ: So he purified it (declared it ritually pure)

ai.seo_question: Is violet oil and gillyflower oil considered ritually pure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly validates the ritual purity (taharah) of violet oil, addressing specific juristic inquiries regarding its status. He further characterizes gillyflower oil (kheiri) as 'latif' (gentle/delicate), a term in Shia jurisprudence often implying a subtle, pure nature suitable for ritual use, thereby reinforcing the permissibility of these scented oils in worship.
